title: Noisy functional as a symmetric pair
statement: Let $n,m\ge0$, $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and let $f,g_1,\ldots,g_m$ be real-valued functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$. Write $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$ and $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, and define $a_{g_j},d_{g_j}$ in the same way from the last-coordinate restrictions. Then $F_P(T_\rho f,(T_\rho g_j)_j)$ equals the uniform expectation over $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ of $L(\rho,c(x))$, with first argument $T_\rho a_f(x)$, second argument $T_\rho d_f(x)$, vector arguments $V(T_\rho a_f,(T_\rho a_{g_j})_j)(x)$ and $V(T_\rho d_f,(T_\rho d_{g_j})_j)(x)$, and $c(x)=(\rho T_\rho d_f(x))^2$.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ is an $m$-tuple of real-valued functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$
replaced: For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, a real function $h$ on a uniform Boolean cube, and a vector $k$ of real functions on that cube, put $V(h,k)(x)=((D_i h(x))_i,(k_j(x))_j)$ and $F_P(h,k)=\mathbb E\sqrt{P(h)^2+\|V(h,k)\|_2^2}$, where $D_i$ is the coordinate half-difference. Let $f$ be a real function and $g$ a vector of $m$ real functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$. Put $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, $g_b(x)=g(x,b)$, $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$, $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, and define $a_g,d_g$ componentwise. Let $T_\rho$ denote Boolean noise with real correlation $\rho$, whose Fourier multiplier on a set of size $k$ is $\rho^k$. For each $x$, put $a=T_\rho a_f(x)$, $b=T_\rho d_f(x)$, $u=V(T_\rho a_f,T_\rho a_g)(x)$, and $v=V(T_\rho d_f,T_\rho d_g)(x)$. Then $F_P(T_\rho f,T_\rho g)=\mathbb E_x\frac12\sum_{\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}}\sqrt{P(a+\epsilon\rho b)^2+(\rho b)^2+\|u+\epsilon\rho v\|_2^2}$.
